problem_markdown: Let $1\le k<n$ with $\gcd(k,n)=1$. Colour $1,\ldots,n-1$ with two colours so that $i,n-i$ always agree and, for $i\ne k$, $i,|i-k|$ agree. Prove all numbers have the same colour.
solutions_markdown:
Let $r_j$ be the least positive residue of $jk$ modulo $n$, for $1\le j\le n-1$. Coprimality makes these a permutation of $1,\ldots,n-1$.

For $1\le j\le n-2$, put $r=r_j,s=r_{j+1}$. If $s=r+k<n$, then $s$ and $s-k=r$ have the same colour. If $s=r+k-n$, then $n-r=k-s>0$. The first rule equates the colours of $r$ and $n-r$; the second equates those of $s$ and $k-s=n-r$. Thus consecutive residues $r_j,r_{j+1}$ always agree. The entire permutation, and hence every number, has one colour.
